read.text:
How to read these

Grey boxes are content; blue marks the ONE main action on each screen, which is always the job's next step. Grey panels under a screen show what opens in place, other states and what the other tabs hold.

Press Play on any artboard with a blue mark: links between screens work (Today → Open → Job → Fix 3 things before sending → Paperwork, and so on).

Data is the demo company (Hartline Remodeling), except the first-run row, drawn with a new company (Ridgeway Tile & Bath). Every screen has its own address, shown under the tabs.

jobnote.text:
Rules these screens follow

1. One main button per screen, the job's next step: Fix N things before sending → Review & send → Choose waiver and send → Send follow-up → Draft pay app → Progress pay app → Finish job.
2. The next two sit beside it with a line saying why; the rest are under More, grouped Bill, Get paid, Close out. Explanations live in (i) help.
3. Status is a word in a pill (Needs paperwork, Blocked, Ready to send, Sent, Paid); the full sentence sits under it.
4. Dates read like Aug 12, 2026.
5. Before any send, the screen lists who gets it, who is copied, the amount and the attachments, and asks first.

queue.text:
Today's list, most urgent first

1. Job's done? (a text or email): Mark done and draft
2. Didn't go out: Send again
3. Ready to send: Review & send (opens Before you send)
4. Waiver due: Review waiver (opens the waiver page)
5. Due soon: the customer's pay-app cutoff is within 5 days and nothing is billed this cycle: Bill progress
6. Needs paperwork or Blocked: Add N missing documents, Fix N things before sending or Get CO N signed
7. Follow up, past the customer's days between follow-ups: Send follow-up, or Spoke to them…
8. Approved: the customer approved it with a date to pay; no button
9. Not billed or Not billed yet: Draft pay app (sends nothing) or Bill progress
10. Inbox item with a suggested job: Add to this job

One next step per job; a cutoff within 5 days is added to that job's row and moves it up. The owners get the same rows by email each morning there is something due.

money.text:
Money is one destination with tabs: Pay apps (with a Paperwork column), Change orders, Unpaid, Payments, Closeout (lien waivers, and held back, still owed), Outbox.

Settings is Company (the details on every pay app and how you bill, which sets the trial: 90 days, or 45 for draws; sending and email; QuickBooks; your data), Team, My account (name, password, two-step sign-in), Billing (charged on the 5th; members see it read-only), Customer settings (with each customer's monthly pay-app cutoff), Activity log (with the hash-chain check), Help, and Helper answers for the founders.

phone.text:
Phone layout

Top bar with a menu button; the five destinations open in a drawer.
Tabs scroll sideways and fade at the right edge.
Every table becomes one card per row, each value labelled; a schedule of values is one card per line.
The main action is full width; on Today the buttons sit under each row's text.
Every control is at least 44 px tall.
The Inbox, the job record and each missing paperwork item have Take a photo, which opens the camera.

newrow.text:
What these add

Results: counted from the company's own pay apps and payments; nothing estimated. A monthly summary email goes to the owner.

Payments: QuickBooks payments are proposed, never recorded until ticked, from a CSV or Excel export or, once connected, from QuickBooks itself (read-only); each is recorded once, and a row with no match gets a pay app to pick. "Check against QuickBooks" lists the differences.

Customer settings: a pay app sent back or a draft the customer wanted changed becomes a suggested paperwork item; nothing changes until Add to paperwork. Each customer shows how long they actually take to pay, with "Use N days" when the setting is off. The pay-app cutoff is a contract date, not a legal one.

Job history, Outbox and Activity log load 50 rows at a time.

outside.text:
Outside the app

The customer page is linked from each pay app email. It shows the job's figures, the lines, the paperwork and the PDF; Mark as received, Approve for payment (with a date) and Send a question update the job.

The signing page is emailed for an unsigned change order. The typed name, consent, time, network address and a fingerprint of what was shown are kept. Counsel should check the consent wording.
